x: Dave Carter performed well to finish 4th in the 220yds final, and Terry Newell and Dave Mitchell both qualified for the final of the 880yds; but nothing of note was produced. 1961 showed us a marked absence of "Claret and Gold".
Dave Mitchell was another to have an off day recording a mediocre 2:1.7. Jim McGrath reached the long jump final and with a leap of 22'3¾" finished sixth.

Another to break a Club record at the same meeting was David Cocks, whose 2:0.8 clocking in the Intermediate 880 final was 0.2 secs inside Dave Mitchell's four year old mark, but was still not good enough to place him in the result!

With half a lap to go in the 880yds, defending champion John Davies looked an odds-on winner, but in the final straight first Terry Newell and then Dave Mitchell sprinted past, leaving a surprised John to finish fourth just behind Bhatia who had made up a tremendous amount of ground in the last 220yds.
Beats Dave Mitchell's 4yr old mark by one fifth of a second. Since setting this new time he has clocked 1:59:0 off scratch in a handicap race, so his official mark is already in danger.
Another to establish a personal best at this event is Dave Mitchell. His 1:55.7 was accomplished with virtually no training - he has just graduated from College.
Graham Worrell (24.2) and Pat Cornelius (24.8) were 3rd and 4th in the furlong, whilst Dave Mitchell (2:6.2) and F. Paget (2:12.0) took 5th and 7th places in the 880 yds.

Former co-editor DAVE MITCHELL writes from Tonbridge, which is sufficiently far away to keep him safe from the 'Harriers'! He is seriously thinking of getting involved in athletics again, but possibly as a coach.

Twentynine years ago at Crystal Palace, and Jim Vivian, Chris Martin, Robert Nelson and Dave Mitchell pose for the camera of Ed. Lacey after placing 6th in the final of the A.A.A. 4 x 220yds relay Championship in 1:31.9.
Also, the caption to the Flashback photograph on page 44 should have referred to John Mitchell, not Dave Mitchell (who was actually a past Joint Editor of this magazine).
